purpose: One row in the sidebar, and the sub-list beneath it. Rendered by AppShell from navItems — you almost never write this yourself.

useInstead.use: AppShell's navItems prop — does the tree need to be data, or is this genuinely one loose row?

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for nav row shape in this package. The rules below are about the NavItem you put in navItems, not about calling this component.
decision.beforeTheRules: Depth is NOT a prop and never will be. SideNavLink reads it from context and adds one for itself, which is what makes the 3-level cap enforceable — a prop would let a caller assert a level it does not occupy.

rules.because: it renders as a link; without one it becomes a pure expand toggle

rules.if: the row is a group with no page of its own
rules.then: give it children and NO href
rules.because: a group that pretends to be a link lands the user on a placeholder; with no href it renders as a <button> that only expands

rules.if: the row both has a page and contains children
rules.then: give it both — it renders an <a> plus a separate expand <button>
rules.because: one control cannot both navigate and expand; two real controls beat one that guesses from click coordinates

rules.if: you are about to nest a fourth level
rules.then: flatten the branch or promote it to its own section
rules.because: there is nowhere for a fourth level to indent to; the component throws a named error in development rather than rendering something broken

rules.if: the row needs a secondary line
rules.then: set `description`, but only at depth 2 or 3
rules.because: depth 1 has to survive collapsing to a 56px rail, where a second line has nowhere to go; set at depth 1 it is ignored and dev builds warn

rules.if: the row needs a count or a status word
rules.then: set `badge` to a number or a node
rules.because: it renders at the trailing edge and hides with the label when the rail collapses

rules.if: the label is long and the icon alone would be ambiguous
rules.because: it shows only while the rail is a 48px strip, where the label is not visible

constraints: Active state is DERIVED from AppShell's currentPath. There is no isActive prop and adding one would let two rows claim the current page.
A parent is active when any descendant matches, which is also what decides which branches start expanded.

accessibility.keyboard: Every row is reachable by Tab. Expand triggers are <button> and respond to Enter and Space; navigation rows are <a>.
accessibility.aria: The current row carries aria-current="page". Expandable rows carry aria-expanded and an aria-controls pointing at their sub-list, which stays in the DOM (hidden) so the reference always resolves.
accessibility.notes: While the rail is collapsed the label is hidden with visibility, not display — it leaves the accessibility tree and the tab order either way, but visibility can be animated, so the label fades instead of popping.

composition.childrenContract: None directly. SideNavLink is rendered by AppShell from a NavItem; its sub-list comes from that item's `children` array, and it renders itself recursively for each one.
composition.notes: The sub-list stays in the DOM when closed (hidden, or at zero height while the rail collapses) so the row's aria-controls always resolves to a real element. Do not unmount it to "clean up" — a dangling aria-controls is worse than none.

antiPatterns.dont: Adding a `level` or `depth` field to a NavItem
antiPatterns.do: Nest it in `children` and let depth be derived
antiPatterns.why: a depth prop can lie, and the 3-level cap would then be unenforceable

antiPatterns.dont: Adding an `isActive` flag to a NavItem
antiPatterns.why: active state is computed from the tree so exactly one row can be current; a flag lets two claim it

antiPatterns.dont: Giving a group row an href that points at its first child
antiPatterns.why: a crumb or row that goes 'up' should not move the user sideways into a sibling; with no href it becomes a pure toggle

antiPatterns.do: Put it on the depth 2 or 3 row it belongs to
antiPatterns.why: it is ignored at depth 1 because the collapsed rail cannot show it

antiPatterns.dont: Nesting four levels because the information architecture has four
antiPatterns.do: Promote the third level to its own NavSection
antiPatterns.why: the component throws rather than rendering an indent that does not exist

incorrect.why: neither field exists — depth comes from nesting and active state from currentPath
if Settings has no page of its own, omit the href; pointing it at a child moves the user sideways
descriptions are ignored at depth 1, because the 56px rail has nowhere to render a second line
